title: Atrium 0.18.0
notes:
The window is AppKit now. The main window, its three columns, the toolbar, the menus, the menu-bar item, the task pane and the two small windows no longer go through SwiftUI. Nothing is meant to look or work differently except the points below.

## What you can notice

- **Column widths are remembered.** The timeline's and the widget column's widths come back after a restart, and a width you chose survives hiding the widgets and resizing the window. Before, every launch began at the default widths while the window's own frame was restored.
- **Double-clicking a divider gives the column its default width back.** The dividers are invisible until the pointer is on them, so a column dragged too far had no other way back.
- **Closing the main window hides it.** Opening it again is immediate, with folded sections and scroll positions where they were. The old window rebuilt its content each time.
- **A solid window is laid out like a translucent one.** With translucency at 0 the title bar is transparent too, the content fills the window, and the middle column has no plate of its own: the three columns follow one rule in both looks.
- **The first row is not under the toolbar buttons.** Content starts below the title bar and fades over its top 12 points once it is scrolled.

## Rebuilt, meant to be the same

The main menu and every shortcut; the menu-bar item; the task header and its session settings; the composer with its completions, attachments and queued messages; pinned work; the editor with its timeline rail; the terminal drawer, filled or not; the scratch terminal and Software Update windows, which open in the middle of the screen and come back where you left them.

Behind a card (a confirmation, Settings, a diff) the timeline and the widget column leave the accessibility tree, as the rest of the window does: VoiceOver stays inside the card.

## Still SwiftUI

A few cards inside the AppKit dialog layer (New Task and Rename among them) and the developer demo pages. The app still links SwiftUI until they are moved.

## Packaging

- The app bundle carries every licence under `ThirdPartyNotices/`. 0.17.6 added them to the repository; its bundle had two.

## Checks

- The real-window checks no longer bring the test app to the front. Keys sent to it are routed, in the test build only, to the window that would be key, typing does not go through the selected input method, and a check fails when the test app became frontmost while it ran. Before this, the checks swallowed the keys of whoever was working at the same Mac and failed when that person typed.
- The icon measurements of 0.17.6 were run with the displays off, where the system reports a 1× screen: the whole UI target passes there as it does at 2×, and the hand probe counts 17 half-point differences from SwiftUI's own layout, the number it counted at 2×.

## Not verified

- **A real agent in the new window.** The real-window checks drive the isolated test app with recorded and simulated agents. No real Claude, Codex or Kiro session has been run through this window yet.
- **The pointer on the dividers.** Dragging a divider and double-clicking it are tested on the real split view with constructed events, not by hand. Two real clicks were made: a button in Software Update and one in the scratch terminal.
- **The active window at 2× on this exact build.** The last pass ran with the displays off, so its screenshots are at 1×; the 2× screenshots that were read came from the shell before its last three merges (0.17.6, the checks' key routing, the fix for cards and the accessibility tree).
- **VoiceOver itself.** What it would read was checked through the accessibility API, not by listening.
- **The app's own icon measurements, row by row, between displays on and off.** Both states pass the same tests; the table taken with the displays on was lost, so the direct comparison waits for a new one.

title: Atrium 0.17.6
notes:
Codex moves to ACP v2, Kiro's own turn data is shown, and icons are laid out the same whichever display the system reports.

## Codex

Codex now talks to Atrium over ACP v2, on the same connection and display model Claude already uses.

- **Model and reasoning effort are two settings.** On v1 Codex offered combined ids (`gpt-6.1-sol[low]`); on v2 they are separate options and use the same pickers as the other agents. A saved preset in the old form is split into the two and applied when both parts still exist; one that no longer matches is dropped and the adapter's default stays.
- **A message sent while a turn runs is a prompt of its own.** It no longer goes through Codex's private steering call. Each message gets the usage of its own part of the turn; when two messages end together their usage is counted once.
- **A plan that streams in as Markdown stays one row.** Codex resends the whole plan on every change; the row is replaced instead of growing a line per update.
- **Stopping a turn keeps its usage**, and the stopped command shows as cancelled.
- **Sessions from 0.17.5 resume.** A Codex session started on v1 continues under v2 with the same id, its settings and its conversation; nothing is replayed twice.
- **Going back.** An adapter that only answers version 1 is used on v1 as before. To force v1 for the built-in Codex: `defaults write io.github.chenkeyv.atrium acp.codexProtocol v1`, then start a new session.

Permission cards, terminal output, file diffs, sub-agents and the chief's own tools look and behave as they did.

## Kiro

Kiro reports more about a turn than Atrium showed. 0.17.5 read the credits; this version reads the rest.

- **A turn's duration is the one Kiro measured**, not Atrium's own clock, and a turn Kiro reports as aborted shows as stopped.
- **The tools a turn used** are listed under its credits when you hover the turn's usage (up to six names, then a count).
- **Permission cards name what Kiro asks about**: its own title for the operation, the resource it applies to and the scope it would be allowed for. A card Kiro asks again replaces the earlier one, and a request Kiro resolves on its side is withdrawn.
- **A turn ends when Kiro says it ended.** Kiro sends `turn_end` before the prompt's own result; Atrium now closes the turn on it, so a late or missing result no longer leaves a finished turn looking as if it were running.

## Layout

- **Icons beside text are measured the same on every display.** AppKit rounds a symbol's box on the pixel grid of the screen the system reports, and the system reports a 1× screen while the displays are off. The same row could be half a point taller or shorter depending on that. Atrium now measures each symbol once at a very large size, scales the box down and puts it on the half-point grid itself.
- **The gap between an icon and its title is the same in every row.** Where a title's start was computed from the icon's width, it could be half a point off the spacing the rest of the app uses.

## Tests

- Layout tests no longer compare against heights that were read off a display, or against whatever SwiftUI lays out on the day. They assert what the layout promises: one baseline for the parts on a line, gaps equal to the spacing tokens, a row as tall as its parts, nothing clipped. The comparison with SwiftUI and the system's own symbol sizes is now a probe run by hand (`scripts/dev/metric-probe.py`, `scripts/dev/symbol-probe.swift`).

## For the open-source release

No change in behaviour: the company gateway's name is gone from code, tests and strings, paths from the development machine are gone from the tree, and the licences of the bundled third-party code were added under `ThirdPartyNotices/`.

## Not verified

- **Icon layout with the displays off.** Every test and the hand probe ran with the displays on, where the system reports a 2× screen. The measurement is built not to depend on that; the run that shows it has not been made yet.
- **Codex on v2 against a real account**: one turn (a command, a file, its usage) on codex-acp 2.6.0. The recorded sessions the tests replay are from 2.5.0. Permission cards, a message sent mid-turn, stopping, resuming a 0.17.5 session, sub-agents and a usage-limit error were tested on those recordings and on a simulated adapter, not live.
- **Kiro**: one real turn on one model. A stopped turn, a failed turn and a resumed session were tested on recordings only. Kiro says it can report a model fallback; none has been seen, so nothing reads one.
- **The third-party licences inside the app bundle**: they are in the repository; whether the packaged app carries them was not checked.

title: Atrium 0.17.5
notes:
The running turn's preview stays on its newest line, a thought no longer cuts into the row below it, and a Kiro turn shows its credits.

## The rolling preview

While a turn runs, the folded tool bar shows a short preview of its latest calls and thoughts. It is meant to stay on the newest line, with older lines fading out at the top.

- **It no longer gets stuck on its first lines.** Scrolling the conversation with the pointer over the preview scrolled the preview itself, to its top, and from then on it stopped following: new calls arrived cut off under the fade at the bottom. Now only a scroll that actually moves the preview pauses it, and it goes back to the newest line when the pointer leaves, three seconds after the last scroll, or when you scroll back to the bottom.
- **The wheel passes through at the ends.** At its top or bottom the preview hands the scroll to the conversation instead of swallowing it. A scroll gesture that began outside the preview keeps scrolling the conversation as the preview passes under the pointer, inertia included.
- **A thought no longer overlaps the next row.** The thought line was measured with the reading font and drawn with the thought font. With a conversation font other than the system, serif or mono ones (Helvetica or Palatino, say), the line was drawn taller than its place and the top of the row below it was cut.

## Kiro

- **A Kiro turn shows the credits it used** beside its duration (0.07 credits, say), and the context widget shows the session's total. Kiro reports both at the end of each turn; 0.17.4 had the place for them but did not read them yet.
- Kiro stays on ACP v1. Kiro 3.1.0 answers a request for protocol version 2 with 2, but a recorded turn shows it still speaks the v1 shapes (the prompt's own result ends the turn, permission requests are v1's), which Atrium's v2 connection does not accept. Nothing is lost by staying: its own fields, credits included, arrive on v1 as well.

## Releases

- The upload to the public releases is bounded and retried: 0.17.4's stalled for 36 minutes and its update feed had to be published by hand.

## Not verified

- Kiro's credits against more than one recorded turn: one real turn on one model was captured. Cancelled and failed turns, sub-agents and a session resumed from history were not.

- A real trackpad on the preview: the wheel rules are tested with constructed events through the real `scrollWheel(with:)` and as a pure decision table, not by hand.

title: Atrium 0.17.4
notes:
The context widget opens to the text behind each of its rows, shows the cache hit rate, and every finished turn says what it used. The built-in Gemini CLI agent is gone. The daemon protocol is 15.

## Context: the text behind a row

The context widget listed what fills an agent's window (system prompt, tools, memory, conversation…) as numbers only.

- **Click a row to read it.** The original text opens under that row, in monospace, selectable, with Copy; text that comes from a file on disk has Open as well. It grows to 240 pt and scrolls beyond that. Click the row again to fold it; only one row is open at a time.
- **What each agent can show:**
  - Atrium's own agent: every row. The text is what its last request to the model carried: the system prompt, memory, the tools' JSON schemas, the pack, the conversation, tool results, and the stand-ins for trimmed output.
  - Claude Code: memory files (read from disk) and messages (the conversation as Atrium recorded it, not the bytes sent to the model). The system prompt, system tools, MCP tools and skills are not exposed by its adapter.
  - Kiro: context files (read from disk), your prompts and Kiro's responses (as Atrium recorded them). Tools, memory and session files are not available.
  - A row an agent does not provide says so in one line; nothing is filled in from elsewhere.
  - Agents that report only a total (Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode) have no rows to open, as before.
- A finished task keeps the rows whose text is a file or the recorded conversation. The Atrium agent's request is gone once its task has ended.
- The browser page cannot ask for this text yet: the daemon refuses the request from a browser connection.

## Cache hit rate

- **"Cache hits N%"** in the context widget, for the last turn: cache reads over everything the turn sent as input. Hover for the three numbers. It was shown for Atrium's own agent only; it now also appears for Claude Code and Codex, whose adapters report cache reads and writes.
- An agent whose numbers could not be checked against a real capture (Antigravity, OpenCode) shows a rate only when it reports zero cache reads. Kiro reports none, so it shows nothing. Nothing is estimated.

## What a turn used

- **Each finished turn shows one number beside its duration**: the agent's own cost when it reports one (Claude Code: this turn's share of the session's cost), otherwise the turn's token total. Hover for input, output, cache reads, cache writes and reasoning, whichever were reported. A turn whose agent reports nothing shows nothing.
- **The session's total** is in the context widget, with the cache hit rate.
- Kiro's credits have a place in the record and in the display, but Atrium does not read them from Kiro yet.

## Agents

- **The built-in Gemini CLI agent is removed**; Antigravity replaces it. Tasks you ran with it still show in the timeline under its name and icon, and a `gemini` entry you wrote yourself in `agents.json` keeps working. Antigravity's Gemini models are unaffected.

## Protocol

- The daemon protocol is 15 (`context/section`). The minimum a client needs is unchanged, so a 0.17.3 app still works against a 0.17.4 daemon; it just cannot open rows.

## Not verified

- Kiro's context files and Claude Code's memory files against the real agents: the sources are tested with their recorded shapes, not with a live Kiro or Claude session.
- Whether Antigravity's input count already includes cache reads: its only real capture has zero cache reads.
- Kiro's credits and Codex's per-turn numbers in a live session.

title: Atrium 0.17.3
notes:
Settings in the borderless look: no card, no sidebar, new motion. The daemon protocol stays at 14.

## Settings

Settings were an opaque card with a darker sidebar inside it, and editing a model service or adding a remote Mac put a second card on top of the first. They are a page on the window's own background now.

- **No card.** Opening Settings (⌘,) blurs and dims the three columns where they are and sets one centred column of rows over them. There is no panel edge, no outline and no title.
- **Tabs are a row of words**: General, Agent, Memory, Remote, with a short accent line under the current one. ⌘1–⌘4 go to a page; with the row focused, ← and → move between pages.
- **Rows without boxes.** A label on the left and its control on the right; groups are separated by space, not by lines or plates. Segmented choices (theme, permissions) are words with a faint capsule under the chosen one; the font size is a number with a pair of arrows; text actions (Edit…, Add, Check for Updates) are accent-coloured words.
- **Second-level pages push in.** Editing a model service, adding a remote Mac and changing the remote password slide into the same column, and the tabs become a breadcrumb. Esc or ‹ goes back one page; Esc again closes Settings. Leaving a form with unsaved changes still asks first.
- **Motion.** Opening fades the veil in while the rows rise into place; changing pages slides the accent line to the new word and moves the old page out and the new one in; the capsule of a segmented choice slides. Closing takes about 180 ms.
- Clicking anywhere outside the column closes Settings, as does the × at the end of the tab row.

The four pages hold the same settings as before, in the same order. The forms on the second-level pages (a model service and its models, a remote Mac) keep their boxed fields for now.

## Tests

- A first round of test clean-up: redundant tests are removed (Core, agent and web suites), tests that returned early without saying so now fail loudly, and assertions on wall-clock time have wider margins. `make test` runs the Python tests too.

## Not verified

- Settings with a real Pinyin input method in the forms' text fields.
- VoiceOver itself: the accessibility tree is checked by scripts (roles, labels, one current page, one navigation group), not by listening to it.

title: Atrium 0.17.2
notes:
One background behind the whole window, a conversation drawn entirely without SwiftUI, and a round of hardening for remote access and updates. The daemon protocol stays at 14.

## One background

In the borderless look each of the three columns painted its own shade. With translucency on, the task list, the conversation and the bar on the right did not match.

- **All three columns share one backdrop now**: one translucent layer and one blur behind the whole window, with no plate of its own under any column.
- **The solid window follows.** The conversation no longer sits on a lighter sheet than its neighbours, and the strip above it is gone.

## The conversation is all AppKit

0.17.0 moved the conversation's rows to AppKit and left four pieces in SwiftUI: the diff card, the running turn's rolling preview of tool output, the tool bar that stays pinned while you scroll, and the empty conversation. These are drawn natively now. The SwiftUI conversation is deleted, and so is the hidden switch between the two. Text is measured without SwiftUI as well. Nothing is meant to look different.

- **Row heights no longer follow the display.** An icon in a tool row was laid out on the screen's pixel grid, so the row could come out one point taller or shorter on a non-Retina display, or while the display slept. Icons are sized on a fixed grid now.
- The tooltip on the auto-approved bolt ("Auto-approved · …") is back on tool rows; the native rows had lost it.

## Limits

- Claude sometimes puts its limit sentence at the end of a longer reply instead of sending it alone (seen with a real weekly limit). That is recognised now, so the task waits and continues as described for 0.17.1 instead of ending as an ordinary reply.

## Remote access and updates

- **Oversized frames before the password are refused from their header.** A connection that has not signed in may send 4 KiB per message. This was checked only after the whole frame had arrived, and the receive buffer allows 256 MiB, so each of the 32 connections allowed to wait for a password could make the Mac hold that much. The length is read from the frame header now and the connection is closed before any of the payload is buffered: masked or not, whatever the frame's type, and whatever length it claims.
- **The updater checks the running app against its signature** before it reads the signer that updates are pinned to. If the app on disk was changed after launch, the update is refused.
- **Switching remotes cannot hang on an old SSH connection.** Stopping a tunnel waits at most about 25 seconds for the previous connection's task; a keychain prompt left open could hold it forever, and every later switch was refused as busy.

## Releases and tests

- Publishing the update feed retries after a network error (0.17.1's feed had to be published by hand after one), and the feed alone can be published again without rebuilding the app.
- Test waits have deadlines, so a condition that never comes true fails the test instead of hanging the run; the mock agent no longer outlives its test; pictures compared in tests are drawn into a fixed bitmap instead of the screen's.

## Not verified

- A real non-Retina display: the row-height fix is checked by drawing at a fixed scale, not on such a screen.
- Memory under a real flood of oversized frames: the tests show the connection is closed from the header, before the payload is sent; they do not measure the process.
- The updater's signature check in a signed release: it first runs for real when 0.17.2 updates to the version after it.

title: Atrium 0.17.1
notes:
Two things. A task that runs into its agent's usage limit now waits for the limit to lift and carries on by itself. And the browser page can act, not only watch: answer a permission, send a message, steer a running turn and stop it. The daemon protocol stays at 14.

## When an agent hits its limit

Until now a turn that stopped on a usage or rate limit was a failed turn like any other, and you had to notice the time and come back.

- **It is its own state.** The task's row says "Limit reached" with what happens next, and the end of the conversation has a small card. The agent's own message stays in the conversation as it was.
- **When the agent said when the limit resets**, Atrium continues the task by itself at that time (a few seconds after, 5 to 30). The row carries an hourglass and reads "Limit reached · continues at 9:40 PM"; the card offers Continue Now and Cancel Automatic Continue. The time is shown in your time zone, whatever zone the agent named.
- **When it did not**, nothing is guessed: the row reads "Limit reached · reset time unknown", the task counts as needing you, and the card offers Continue Now and Dismiss. The same after you cancel the automatic continue.
- **What continuing sends**: if the turn had already started working, the one line "Continue from where you stopped."; if it had not, your last message again. Messages you queued go first.
- **You can always just type.** Sending a message leaves the state and cancels the timer.
- **It stops trying**: if the continue runs into the limit again, that counts; after three in a row the task waits for you. A reset time that is not at least half a minute ahead after a failed continue is not trusted.
- **It survives a restart.** The timer is part of the task: after an update or a restart of the background service the task is still waiting for the same time and continues once. A task whose time passed more than a day ago while nothing was running waits for you instead. A task you reopen from history never sends anything by itself.
- **Recognising a limit**: Claude's message ("You've hit your 5-hour limit · resets 5:30pm (Asia/Shanghai)") was checked against a real one, including the case where Claude reports it as an ordinary end of turn. The patterns for Codex, Antigravity and Kiro come from their documentation and reports, not from limits we hit ourselves; one that is missed still shows as a failed turn, as before. Every failed turn now keeps its raw error in the task's log, so a missed pattern can be added from it.
- An older Atrium connected to the same background service, and the browser page, see such a task as idle with a failed last turn.
- **Handoff summaries** (when a task is continued in a new session or by another agent) now always keep the original request, then the latest exchanges, one line of changed files and the results of the last commands, and say how many earlier messages were left out.

## In the browser

The server side of this shipped in 0.16.4; this is the page. Open `https://<your Mac>:<port>/` with remote access on, as before, and sign in with the remote access password.

- **Permissions**: a task that is waiting shows its request as a card with the same choices the Mac offers. Tap one and the turn goes on. If the Mac (or the chief agent) answered first, the card says who did and what was chosen. A long detail scrolls inside the card and keeps its line breaks; with several requests waiting the card says how many are left.
- **Messages**: a box at the bottom of a task. While the task is idle it sends a message; while a turn is running the same box steers it, and what you sent is listed above the box as waiting for the model or waiting for the turn to end. A message still waiting can be taken back with ×.
- **Stop**: a round button beside the box while a turn is running (Esc with a keyboard). It ends the turn and leaves what you were typing.
- **A dropped connection while sending** does not send twice and does not lose the text. The page says it is checking, and when the connection is back it either clears the box (the message arrived) or says it did not arrive and can be sent again; sending again reuses the same message id, so the daemon takes it once.
- **Drafts** are kept per task while the page is open and cleared when you sign out.
- **Signing in once is enough**: a new tab, or a tab the phone had put away, opens straight to your tasks while the sign-in is still valid (seven days). Before, every new tab asked for the password again.
- With a keyboard, Return sends and Shift-Return starts a new line; a Return that confirms input-method composition is not taken for send. On a phone the box stays above the keyboard and focusing it does not zoom the page.
- Everything a browser does is written into the task on the Mac as a line of its own ("Message from a browser", "Allowed from a browser", "Stopped from a browser"), as since 0.16.4.

## What the browser still cannot do

Start, close or delete a task, open a terminal, browse files or diffs, change mode, model, permission level or the fence, change settings, or attach images. The page does not work offline. A browser is limited to 20 writes in a burst and one every 2 seconds after that; past it the page says how long to wait.

One thing to know: the remote access password is the only thing between a browser and these actions. There is no second confirmation on the Mac for a message or an answer sent from a browser; each one is visible in the task afterwards.

## Smaller changes

- CI no longer uploads a copy of the app for every run (only when started by hand, kept one day); the uploads had filled the account's artifact storage.

## Not verified

- A real limit from Codex, Antigravity or Kiro; only Claude's wording comes from a real sample.
- In the browser: what the page says while the Mac does not answer and while the phone is offline (the check would have needed to suspend the server), Return during input-method composition, the Chinese wording on the page, and a real iPhone with its keyboard up.

title: Atrium 0.17.0
notes:
The main window is now drawn by AppKit: the timeline, the conversation and the widget column, and with them Settings and every card. It looks the same and does the same things, and selects a task in about half the time. The composer learns to complete: ranked slash commands, `@` file paths, and a grey word that finishes the one you are typing.

## The window

- **Conversation**: turns are native rows, made only near what is on screen, with their text laid out off the main thread. A running turn streams in the same row it ends in, so nothing is swapped when it finishes. Inline code sits on a rounded background the height of its letters; a full line of Kaiti keeps its own line height; resizing the window keeps the old layout until the new one is ready.
- **Copy**: the context menu on a prompt, a reply, a tool row or a thought has "Copy This Item" and "Copy Turn as Markdown" (the prompt quoted, then each reply). ⌘A in a text block selects that block; with the conversation itself focused it marks the turns in view, and ⌘C copies them as Markdown.
- **Timeline**: the same rows, lanes and forks, drawn by one view that makes rows only for what is visible. Rows no longer slide under the toolbar's buttons when the list scrolls. With a range selected, Esc clears the range first and ⌘[ / ⌘] step it; ⌘⌫ deletes the selected task only while the timeline has the keyboard.
- **Widget column**: a file row you click is visibly selected, and hovering shows which row you are on. Click selects and shows the change; ⌘-click or a double-click opens the file. Space (Quick Look) and Return (open in the editor) act only while the list has the keyboard, so a space typed in the terminal drawer or the editor is no longer taken for Quick Look. While an agent is streaming, "Changed by this task" is recomputed at most twice a second, off the main thread, and at once when the turn ends.
- **Diff card**: the card a changed file opens is native; it takes the keyboard for the table once the diff has arrived.
- **Softer edges**: the side columns sit on a plate a shade apart from the conversation and fade into it over 16 pt; nothing is ruled under the range strip or after a day marker, and cards have no border. The thin lines where the columns can be dragged are still there; they go when the window's frame itself moves to AppKit, which is next.
- **Window buttons on the right**: New Task, Next Blocked Task, Close Details and Widgets moved from beside the traffic lights to the top-right corner, where they no longer sit over the timeline's first row.
- For this version the previous SwiftUI conversation can still be selected for comparison with the hidden preference `conversation.engine` (`swiftui`); it goes in the next.

## Settings and cards

- **Settings is four pages**: General, Agent, Memory, Remote, about 25 controls in all. Translucency is one slider that reads as transparency (0 is opaque, up to 85%); a translucent window always blurs what is behind it. Each agent has one pop-up for which model it may hand work to. Remote access is one switch; which networks it listens on (Tailscale, the local network, Surge Ponte) is chosen for you.
- The switches for spell checking and the system's inline predictions are no longer in Settings. They keep the values you had (both on by default); a place for them beside the composer is not in this version.
- **Cards** (new task, permission, rename, delete, unsaved changes, ssh and direct-connection prompts, the remote and provider forms) are drawn in the window on one layer: Tab stays inside the card, Esc closes it, and the keyboard goes back to where it was. While a card is open the columns behind it are hidden from accessibility and ignore ⌘⌫ and Return.

## Composer

- **Slash commands** are ranked: an exact name, then a prefix, then letters in order, then a match in the description only. Ties go to the command you send most. A row matched only by its description never takes Return (Return sends what you typed; arrow down to choose it). Several matches in one namespace fold into one `ns:` row. After a command and a space, its argument hint shows in grey.
- **`@` paths**: `@` lists the folder's entries at once, and a ranked search of the whole working folder replaces them when it arrives (within 150 ms it is shown directly). The search follows `.gitignore`. A file is inserted with a space after it, a folder with a `/` and the list stays open; names with spaces are quoted. `../`, `~/` and absolute paths list one folder. A remote task lists one level.
- **Grey word**: as you type, the rest of the word may appear in grey from what you have sent before in Atrium. Tab takes it with a space (swallowed again by closing punctuation), → takes it without, Return always sends exactly what you typed. It stays away from code, paths, the command line, an open list and text being composed by an input method. The model is a small file on this Mac (at most 2 MB), never sent anywhere; Settings › Memory › Clear… removes it too.

## Measured

Harness fixtures, 10 presses per target, median / p90 in ms, press to the title on screen and to the title readable through accessibility (the conversation in place). Same checks and limits as v0.16.3.

| Selecting | v0.16.3 | v0.17.0 |
|---|---|---|
| A small past task | 79 / 83, then 153 / 159 | 29 / 37, then 61 / 68 |
| A running task | 71 / 76, then 116 / 122 | 49 / 56, then 51 / 58 |
| A large past task (122 MB log) | 46 / 51, then 93 / 110 | 31 / 31, then 37 / 46 |

The v0.16.3 figures were taken while other branches were building on the same Mac and the v0.17.0 ones on a quieter machine, so part of the difference is load. On the same machine at the same time, the AppKit conversation against the SwiftUI one: 48 against 58 ms to a running task's title, 30 against 37 ms to a small past task's, 176 against 187 MB resident with the everyday fixture; a large history is the same within noise (34 against 33 ms, 339 against 336 MB).

One number misses its target: the highlight of a newly selected timeline row is drawn a median of 27 ms after the press; the design asked for 4.

## Fixed along the way

- Cards still written in SwiftUI (Add Remote, the provider editor) had no accessibility tree at all.
- Pop-up buttons in Settings and the New Task card cut their titles ("Sy…") and, once wide enough, showed two chevrons.
- A table in a reply lost the last character of every cell.
- Settings switches were buttons to accessibility; "Remove" was enabled for the Mac you are connected to.
- The longest label on the General page was cut to "Conversation…".

## Not verified

- Selecting a file row with a real mouse click in the running app, and Space and Return on it afterwards: the logic is unit-tested and the accessibility press opens the diff card, but the harness cannot click without moving your pointer. The Quick Look panel itself was not observed.
- VoiceOver on the new rows; the checks read the accessibility tree, they do not listen.
- The diff card's empty states (binary file, too large, no changes) in the running app.
- `check-subagent-expand.py` fails in the harness because its fixture's mock model is not in the list a worker may use; it was not re-run against v0.16.4 to prove the failure is older than this version. `check-translucency.py` needs a demo build and was not run.
- The widget column's own timing lines (`widgets_shown`, `widget_stats`) and the AppKit timeline's performance gates in a Release build.

title: Atrium 0.16.4
notes:
A security release. An update must now be signed by the same identity as the Atrium that installs it, a browser signed in with the remote password can do less than before and leaves a trace of what it does, and several ways a faulty or hostile peer could crash or stall the app are closed. Nothing changes in how you use the Mac app. The daemon protocol stays at 14.

## Updates

- **Signer check**: before an update is installed, its code signature must satisfy the designated requirement of the Atrium that is running (the same signing identity). An update signed by anyone else is refused with "The update isn't signed by the same developer as this copy of Atrium", and nothing is staged. Until now the updater checked the download's checksum, bundle id, version and that the signature was intact, all of which a replaced release could satisfy.
- Development builds are ad-hoc signed and have no identity to pin, so they update as before.
- If Atrium ever changes its signing identity or bundle identifier, the first version under the new one has to be installed by hand; the message points to the release page.

## Remote access and the browser

The browser page is still read-only in this version, but the server used to accept more from a signed-in browser than the page ever sent. Now:

- **Fewer methods**: a browser connection may call 16 methods: reading and syncing state, sending, queueing and steering a message, cancelling a turn or a queued message, answering a permission request, and the read methods for history, folders and diffs. Closing, stopping or finishing a task, changing its mode or options, continuing a past task and stopping background work are refused (`-32003`). The Mac app connecting directly keeps everything it had.
- **A browser is always a browser**: a connection that carries an `Origin` header or signs in with the cookie gets the browser's method set whatever it says about itself.
- **No remote connection answers as the chief**: a permission answered with `answeredBy: "chief"` over a remote connection is refused; that identity belongs to the chief agent's own tool connection.
- **Write budget**: all browser connections together may send 20 writes at once and one more every 2 seconds; beyond that a write is refused with `-32012` and the seconds to wait. Reconnecting does not refill it.
- **Sent once**: `session/queue` with a `messageID` the daemon has already seen answers with success and does nothing, so a page that resends after a dropped connection cannot double a message. `session/steer` takes a `messageID` too.
- **A trace on the Mac**: a message, a permission answer, a stop and a cancelled queued message that came from a browser each add a one-line notice to the task's transcript ("Allowed from a browser", "Message from a browser", …). A permission answer records that it came from the web.
- **Sign out closes the connection**: signing out ends every socket opened with that cookie, not only the cookie. A cookie is checked again once its socket is registered.
- **Smaller frames**: a browser frame, whole or in fragments, is limited to 1 MiB and the connection is closed with 1009 beyond it.
- **Agent text cannot draw controls**: the page's Markdown sanitizer no longer lets through inline styles, or `input`, `button`, `textarea`, `select`, `label` and `form` elements, which an agent's message could have used to paint over the page.
- The server picks up a new `index.html` without a restart, and keeps the old one if the new one cannot be read.

## Fixes

- **Duplicate ids no longer crash the app**: a snapshot from a faulty or remote daemon that repeats a session or lane id used to trap in three places (session order, the timeline graph); the first entry now wins.
- **Switching the remote host does not freeze the window**: ending the old ssh tunnel could hold the main thread for up to five seconds. It now ends in the background, and the new connection starts only when the old one is gone.
- **Atrium's own agent**: opening or loading a session no longer blocks the agent's message loop while provider model lists are fetched, so closing the session during that time is noticed at once; requests for a session that is still loading are refused instead of landing on its previous state; each secret is kept once in the redaction list.

## Not verified

- The signer check on a real update between two published versions through the in-app updater. It was checked with the same Security calls on the published 0.16.1 and 0.16.2 bundles (accepted) and on an ad-hoc build (refused).
- A browser on a phone against a real Mac; the checks ran against the isolated test daemon and server.
- A real ssh server when switching hosts; the tunnel tests use a scripted ssh.

title: Atrium 0.16.3
notes:
Opening a past task is faster and no longer a blank wait. The task's header shows the moment you select it, and the conversation opens at its newest turn instead of reading the whole log first. The "Atrium" title no longer prints over the timeline.

## UI

- **History opens header first**: selecting a past task shows its title, agent and folder right away from what the timeline already knows; only a thin progress line sits where the conversation will be, instead of a large spinner over everything.
- **Newest turn first**: the conversation opens at the end of the log. Older turns load a page at a time when you scroll to the top, and each page adds only its own turns, so the rows already on screen are not rebuilt.
- **Active task**: the composer's text field is built one tick after the conversation's first frame, so selecting a running task paints sooner. The empty field keeps its size, so nothing moves.
- **Selection**: pressing a task selects it in one update; before, the previous task's inspector was rendered once more first (about 10 ms).
- **Window title**: the main window no longer draws "Atrium" in the transparent title bar, where it landed on the first row's icon and title once the timeline scrolled. The window keeps its name for Mission Control, the Window menu and accessibility.
- **Widgets for history**: "Changed by this task" for a past task comes from its recorded files, not from a scan of the whole transcript.

## Measured

Harness fixtures, dark with the translucent window, on a Mac that was also building other branches, 10 presses per target, press → title on screen through AX (so including the AX polling and tree walk):

| Selecting | Before (audit) | Now, median / p90 |
|---|---|---|
| A large past task (`big-history`, 122 MB log) | 870–1225 ms (193 MB log) | 83 / 103 ms |
| A running task (`everyday`) | 340–360 ms to the composer | about 101 / 115 ms to the title |
| A small past task (`everyday`) | 140–190 ms | 145–159 / 147–166 ms (two runs; no faster) |

The daemon serves the newest page of a large log in a median of about 28 ms once the log is in its history list. The before figures are from a different, larger real history, so the large-task row is not a like-for-like comparison; the 150 000-item case was not measured.

The AX figure is "title drawn + the app's next main-thread job": the title can only be read when the main thread answers AX. With the header first, a small past task's title is drawn about 80 ms after the press; the newest page arrives right after and takes another 60–90 ms to lay out, and the AX read waits for it. A running task draws its title at about 72 ms, a large past task at about 43 ms. The polling itself costs about 2 ms. Measured with temporary stamps in the test app and with the harness's new breakdown, on a loaded Mac (other agents building, load average 5–13): small past task 158–171 ms in three runs, of which 85–89 ms until the app first answers and 67–88 ms waiting for the page's layout; running task 96–106 ms; large past task 80 / 102 ms. The harness check now holds the title (the app's first answer) to 150 ms for a small past task and 250 ms otherwise, and the readable-through-AX time to 250 ms for all three; before, the 150 ms limit sat on the second number.

## Remote

- `history/load` takes two optional parameters, `direction` (`forward` by default, or `backward`) and `pageSize` (1 to 500, replacing `limit`). Browsers and the Mac app over the remote tunnel get exactly the pages a local app gets. No protocol bump: an older daemon ignores them and returns forward pages, and the app falls back to reading forward as before.

## Under the hood

- Backward pages start on a user turn, so each page holds whole turns (usually at least the page size); `nextOffset` points at the next older page and is omitted at the start of the log.
- Turns are cached per turn (`ConversationTurnCache`) with a content version; a page, an edit or a new turn re-segments only what changed, and the result equals segmenting the whole transcript.
- The composer measures its line height once per font instead of building a layout manager on every probe.
- Harness: `check-latency.py` (selection latency on `everyday` and `big-history`) and `ax-client presswait`, which also report what each figure is made of (until the app first answers, waiting for its later work, the polling itself); the composer, nvim, ligature and type-scale checks find the timeline by its accessibility label instead of a fixed path, which moved when the range strip became optional; `check-type-scale` shoots the widget column while a task is selected.
- New tests: backward paging and turn boundaries, remote clients paging like the app, incremental segmentation equal to full segmentation, the history header before the first page, the timeline selection reaching the store at once.

title: Atrium 0.16.2
notes:
A quieter, tidier release. Idle CPU drops to about zero, four flaky tests are stable, demo pages leave the shipped binary, and a batch of UI details land: settings card that follows the window, a timeline that never shows adapter stderr as a headline, command-click to open changed files, a green focus ring instead of the system blue one. Atrium's own agent now treats an output-limit cut as a truncated reply instead of an error.

## UI

- **Settings card follows the window**: width min(760, window − 160), height min(720, window − 140), never smaller than 520 × 400.
- **Timeline headlines**: an agent that exits between turns shows its last message (or "Ended"); the adapter's stderr stays in the detail, not in the list.
- **Idle at rest**: the timeline redraws only when a counting label is about to change (every second for the first minute, then every minute), not once a second for the whole column. Idle CPU with a history task selected: about 1.7 % → about 0.1 %.
- **Changed files**: click shows the diff, ⌘-click or Return opens the file in the editor; Space still quick-looks.
- **Focus**: text fields show a 1 pt accent outline instead of the system focus ring (composer, new task, rename, SSH prompts).
- **Tool summary chips**: 13 pt secondary icons, failures stay red, the duplicate thoughts count is gone, help texts are full words.
- **Range strip** appears only with more than a month of history; non-running bars are tertiary.
- **Turn timer** uses a clock icon at 11 pt with "Last turn's time" / "This turn's time" help; the empty detail pane hints at ⌘N.

## Atrium agent

- A `response.incomplete` with reason `max_output_tokens` ends the turn as a truncated reply: text, thoughts and usage are kept, and the reply is continued (up to four continuations) instead of failing.
- Output budget follows effort for OpenAI-style providers: low 8 K, medium 16 K, high 32 K, xhigh/max 64 K, capped by the model's `maxOutputTokens`. Background requests (memory, summary, titles) run at low effort with their own budget.
- A subtask that runs out of continuations returns its partial text with a note instead of an error.
- The system prompt tells the agent not to poll with `sleep`: use `gh run watch`, `wait` or `tail --pid`, and wait at most ten minutes per command.

## Under the hood

- Dead code removed: `TranscriptViews`, `NvimProcess.locate`, unused `ToolSummary` fields and the segmenter's test-result extractor, `SettingsView.Page.visible`; 13 orphaned strings pruned from the catalogs.
- Demo pages and entry points compile only with `-DATRIUM_DEMO`; the shipped binary carries none of them (demo scripts pass the flag).
- Four flaky tests stabilized (session deletion, daemon file debounce, content height layout, turn timer); each ran 10/10 locally.
- Makefile computes the SwiftPM bin path once and builds all products with one `swift build`. CI skips the strict pool on pull requests and keeps the real-app harness out of CI (it opens windows on the self-hosted Mac).
- Docs: design status, README highlights and build prerequisites, testing home wording.

title: Atrium 0.16.1
notes:
Only the Atrium app, the Mac app's own remote relay and a properly scoped MCP client can now talk to the daemon. A fenced agent cannot reach the daemon socket, and a chief agent's MCP connection sees and controls only its own workers. Daemon protocol 14.

## Daemon identity

- The daemon writes an `app-token` file (mode 0600) next to its socket each time it starts listening. The Mac app reads it and presents it in `initialize`; a connection that claims to be the app without the right token is refused with `-32004` and closed.
- Older clients (protocol 13 and below) that present no token are read-only: `initialize`, `state/*`, `history/*` and `fs/tree` work, everything else is refused. Upgrading the app and the daemon together is unaffected.
- Over an SSH remote the app fetches the remote Mac's `app-token` through the main connection before it opens the forwarded socket, and fetches it again when the remote daemon restarts while the ssh connection stays up.
- A socket forwarded by hand (`ATRIUM_SOCKET` / `daemon.socketPath`) needs a copy of the remote `app-token` beside it; `docs/remote.md` shows the two commands.

## Fence

- The Seatbelt fence now denies outbound connections to the daemon socket and the terminal socket, and denies reading or writing `app-token`. A fenced Atrium agent can no longer drive the daemon from inside a task.

## MCP scope

- `atrium-mcp` must present the chief session it serves. The daemon checks that the session exists, is a chief and is allowed to direct workers; otherwise the connection is refused.
- Every session method on that connection must target one of the chief's own workers (including workers already closed into history); anything else is `-32003`. `session/create_related` may only attach to the chief itself.
- Permission answers from an MCP connection must say `answeredBy: "chief"`.
- Snapshots and change notifications sent to an MCP connection contain only the chief and its workers, their history and their terminals.

## Under the hood

- Daemon protocol 13 → 14 (`appIdentityVersion`, `notAnAppCode`). The minimum accepted version stays 6.
- `scripts/test-app/common.py` reads `app-token` for harness RPC; forwarded-socket scenarios pass `home=` explicitly. The remote simulation publishes the remote daemon's token beside the forwarded socket (`remote_sim.publish_token`), since Seatbelt hides the remote home from the app and its fake ssh.
- New tests: `DaemonIdentityTests` (token, read-only fallback, token rotation on restart, fence paths, MCP scope); `SandboxTests` covers the socket and token denials. Existing MCP-based tests create a real chief.
- `docs/daemon.md` and `docs/design.md` D7 describe the token, the read-only fallback, the MCP rules and the fence additions.

title: Atrium 0.16.0
notes:
The first web client. A phone or any browser on your Tailscale network, your LAN or a Surge Ponte link can open the Mac's remote access port, sign in with the remote access password and follow every task live: the task list, the conversation as it streams, thoughts, tool calls, plans and the permission the agent is waiting on. It is read-only in this release; answering and typing still happen on the Mac.

## Web client (W0)

- **Settings › Remote › Allow remote access** now also serves a page at `https://<host>:<port>/`. Sign in once with the remote access password; the browser keeps a session cookie for seven days. Changing the password or turning remote access off signs every browser out.
- Mobile first: a task list sorted by what needs you, then running, then to review; a conversation view that follows the newest content and offers a "New" pill when you have scrolled up; a permission card that shows what the agent asks and the options, with a note that the answer is given on the Mac.
- English and Simplified Chinese, following the browser's language. Dark and light follow the system.
- The page is built from `web/` (Svelte 5, Vite) at release time and shipped inside the app bundle. There is no Node dependency on the Mac.
- Browsers do not trust the self-signed certificate yet: accept the warning once, or wait for certificate import in a later release.

## Remote access hardening

- Before a client has signed in: the TLS and HTTP handshake must finish within 10 seconds, text frames are capped at 4 KiB, at most 32 unauthenticated connections are held, and a ninth signed-in connection is refused on its own instead of closing everyone.
- Password lockout counts an attempt before the hash is checked, so parallel guesses no longer slip past the limit; IPv6 sources are grouped by /64; a successful login no longer resets the whole loopback bucket.
- Browser connections get a smaller set of daemon methods than the Mac app: they can read, send prompts, answer permissions and read files and git, but cannot open terminals, create tasks or change the fence. Binary frames from a browser are refused.
- WebSocket messages split into several frames are reassembled.
- New password hashes use 600 000 PBKDF2 rounds through CommonCrypto; existing hashes keep verifying with their stored round count.
- `Origin` is checked on every browser request; cross-site login or WebSocket attempts are refused.

## Under the hood

- Daemon protocol stays 13. The daemon learns which remote connections are browsers (`remoteKind`) and documents that a client must acknowledge the welcome snapshot before any change is pushed.
- `atrium-remote` gained `--web <dir>`, static file serving with cache and security headers, `POST /login` and `POST /logout`.
- New tests: `RemoteWebTests`, `RemoteHardeningTests`, and 33 web unit tests (`npm test` in `web/`).

## Not yet

- Typing, stopping and answering permissions from the browser (W1); terminal, folder tree, diffs and history transcripts (W2).
- Certificate import or Tailscale certificates for the web page.

title: Atrium 0.15.1
notes:
Remote access grew up: Atrium now finds other Macs on your network, keeps the port open after you log in, and switches between this Mac and a remote without relaunching the app.

## Finding a Mac

- **Settings › Remote › +** now lists the Macs on the local network that offer Atrium remote access (Bonjour `_atrium._tcp`). Picking one fills in its name and address.
- The password is still yours to type, and the host's certificate fingerprint is still confirmed on the first connection. The fingerprint advertised on the network is only a hint, never the trust decision.
- The service includes the Atrium and daemon protocol versions, so an old peer is visible as such rather than silently failing.
- Only Macs that listen on the local network advertise; a Tailscale-only or Surge Ponte-only host does not. macOS asks once for local-network access.

## Remote access after login

- **Settings › Remote › After Login.** With remote access on, this installs a per-user LaunchAgent that starts `atriumd --idle-timeout 0` at login. Remote access works without opening the app.
- Turning remote access off removes it. If the app is moved or updated, the next launch rewrites the plist with the new path and version.
- `--idle-timeout 0` means never exit for being idle. The daemon still exits on an explicit shutdown, and launchd restarts it only after a crash.

## Switching without relaunching

- **Connect / Disconnect** on a remote now rebinds the running app's daemon connection in place. The window, its size, the menu bar and the running process stay; the remote's tasks appear, and switching back reloads this Mac's tasks.
- SSH and direct remotes both benefit. The old daemon keeps running: its agents are not stopped, so nothing is lost if you switch back.
- Editors with unsaved buffers are asked to save or discard first; their instances are closed before the paths change. Terminals and delivered permission notifications belong to the daemon being left behind and are cleared.

## Fixes

- A direct connection's TLS now verifies the certificate without also requiring a hostname match. Connecting by IP, `.ts.net` name or `.sgponte` name works; the pinned fingerprint remains the identity check.
- After a network drop, a direct tunnel returns to "Connected" when a connection gets through again instead of staying on its last error. A wrong password or a changed certificate still stops and waits for you.

## Under the hood

- Daemon protocol stays 13; the three R2 features add no RPC shape.
- `atrium-remote` advertises `_atrium._tcp` with TXT `v=1`, `proto`, `app` and `fp`; the app browses it only while the Add Remote card is open.
- The harness covers the three features with `check-remote-r2.py`: a discovered host, a switch that keeps the app's PID and window, and a LaunchAgent plist whose command starts a daemon that a direct client reaches after the app is gone. The existing SSH-remote checks were updated for in-place switching.

## Not yet

- No discovery over Tailscale (Bonjour does not cross it), no web client yet, and still no public exposure or relay.
- The real local-network permission prompt and a real Tailscale/Ponte network were not exercised in this release; the loopback and rendezvous paths are what the tests cover.

title: Atrium 0.15.0
notes:
Atrium can now be reached directly: a Mac running Atrium offers its daemon over TLS on Tailscale, the local network or a Surge Ponte name, and another Atrium connects with an address and a password — no ssh, no keys, no port forwarding. The same connection carries conversations, terminals and file reads, so remote tasks look like local ones.

## On the host Mac

- **Settings › Remote › Allow remote access.** A switch, a port (7443 by default) and three places to listen: Tailscale, the local network, and Surge Ponte (loopback). Nothing is exposed beyond those.
- **One password.** Set it, or generate one and copy it; it is shown once. Changing it disconnects everyone already connected, and a client must not reconnect on its own.
- **A pinned certificate.** Atrium generates a self-signed certificate on first use and shows its SHA-256 fingerprint. The other Mac pins that fingerprint on first connection, so a changed certificate is refused rather than trusted.
- **Guesses are throttled.** Five wrong passwords from one address lock it for 30 seconds, doubling up to half an hour.
- **What is connected.** The section lists live connections with their source and time, and can drop them all.

## On the connecting Mac

- **Settings › Remote › +** now asks for SSH or direct. A direct remote takes `host:port` and the password; the first connection shows the host's fingerprint to accept.
- Everything else behaves as before: the row shows the host, its state and where it points, and tasks on it read files, run terminals and answer permissions through the same code as an SSH remote.

## Under the hood

- A new `atrium-remote` helper sits beside `atriumd`: TLS 1.3, a WebSocket on `/`, the password check, and a bridge into the daemon's own socket. The daemon supervises it and is the only thing that can configure it.
- Daemon protocol 13 adds `remote/status`, `remote/set_config` and `remote/disconnect_all`. A connection that came in over the remote port is an ordinary session client: it cannot change remote settings, start workers, or stop the daemon.

## Not yet

- Discovery on the local network, keeping remote access on after logout (a LaunchAgent), and switching remotes without relaunching are the next step.
- The phone-friendly web client comes after that.
- Nothing listens on the public internet, and there is no relay.
- Tailscale and Surge Ponte were not exercised on real networks for this release; the loopback path is what the tests cover.

title: Atrium 0.14.1
notes:
Atrium can now send pictures to an agent, and show a file without leaving the app. Pictures pasted, dropped or picked in the composer travel with the prompt, appear in the conversation, and reach the agent in the format it asks for; a file selected in the folder tree opens in Quick Look with Space.

## Sending pictures

- **Three ways in.** The paperclip beside the composer (⌘⇧A), a paste into the field, or a dropped image file. Each picture is shown above the field as a 48 pt thumbnail you can remove before sending.
- **Only where they work.** The composer offers pictures when the agent says it takes them (`promptCapabilities.image`). Claude Code does; the Atrium agent now does too. An agent without that capability gets no paperclip, and a pasted picture is refused with a line saying why.
- **Small and plain.** Pictures are turned upright, scaled to at most 1568 px on the long side and re-encoded (PNG when they have transparency, JPEG otherwise), so EXIF and location data never leave the Mac. One message carries up to eight pictures of 20 MB each.
- **In the conversation.** A sent prompt shows its pictures in a 96 pt strip above its text; click one to see it full size.

## The Atrium agent takes pictures

The built-in agent hands images to Anthropic and OpenAI models in each provider's own shape (an `image` block with base64 `source`, an `image_url` part, or an `input_image` item), and keeps them in its history so a continued session still has them.

## Quick Look

- **Space opens the selected file** in the folder tree, or in "Changed by this task". HTML, images, PDFs and Markdown open in the system's preview; the person's typing is never intercepted.
- The same panel shows a composer thumbnail at full size.

## Under the hood

- The daemon speaks protocol 12: `session/prompt` may carry `attachments`, which the daemon stores beside the session log and forwards as ACP image blocks. Snapshots say whether the agent takes pictures, so an older daemon is never offered any.

## Not yet

- Pictures go out with a prompt of their own: while a turn runs, steering and the queue still carry text only.
- An image an agent posts back still reads as `[image]` in its reply.
- Quick Look in a remote task waits for a file-read request over the daemon (protocol 9 has folder listings but not file contents), so it is local-only for now.

title: Atrium 0.14.0
notes:
Claude Code tasks now run on ACP v2, the newer version of the protocol Atrium speaks to agents. The most visible result: background commands Claude starts now show up in Atrium, with their live output, and you can stop them. Other agents (Codex, Kiro, Antigravity, Gemini, OpenCode, the Atrium agent) are unchanged and stay on v1.

## Background work

- **Pinned above the composer.** Work Claude keeps running in the background is pinned as its own row, with how long it has been running:
  - a command run in the background (`run_in_background`), titled with the command;
  - other background tool work.
- **Live output.** Open a background command's row to see its last lines, updated as it prints.
- **Stop.** A row the agent can stop has a stop button. The row ends when Claude reports it ended, not when you click, so what it shows is what really happened.
- **Claude's own turns.** When a background task finishes, Claude sometimes picks the conversation up again on its own. While it does, a quiet "Claude is working" row is pinned, and its reply lands in the conversation. The task stays idle the whole time: it isn't shown as running, and it never says it needs you.
- **Sidebar.** An idle task with background work still running shows a quiet dot and the count next to its status, for example "2 background tasks running".
- The Monitor tool isn't shown yet: the current adapter (0.101) reports it as done right away and never lists it as running.

## Conversation

- **Edits show real line numbers.** Claude's edit cards and the file view of its changes are drawn from the patch Claude reports, with the file's own line numbers and a gap between separate hunks.
- **Permission requests explain themselves.** When Claude says why it is asking, the reason is on the permission card.
- **Messages sent during a turn.** Claude Code takes a message you send mid-turn at its next stopping point, usually when the current tool finishes. In our side-by-side test this was as quick as before: the message took effect about 5 seconds after it was sent in both versions, once the command it was waiting on finished. The difference is during a long stretch of writing with no tool in between: v2 waits for that stretch to end.

## Compatibility

- Background service protocol 10 → 11.
- An older app connected to this background service sees background rows without the stop button.
- If a future Claude Code adapter breaks v2, Atrium can be sent back to v1 without an update: `defaults write io.github.chenkeyv.atrium acp.claudeProtocol v1`, then restart Claude tasks. An adapter that only speaks v1 is detected and restarted on v1 automatically.
- Claude sessions started on earlier versions continue on v2 with the same history.

## Tests

- **Unit tests:**
  - Both real Claude Code v2 recordings (manual approval and auto mode) replayed into a task: transcript, diffs, permissions, sub-agent, turn ends, background work appearing and stopping, live output, Claude's own turns staying idle.
  - Every kind of v2 message, one by one.
  - Falling back to v1.
  - The v1 preference.
  - Resuming with and without replay.
  - A session started on v1 resuming on v2.
  - Worker rules on v2.
  - Stop forwarded by the background service, refused for agents, hidden for older apps.
  - The other agents stay on v1.
- **Full test suite:** passes in both modes, 1665 tests each.
- **Real-app screenshot checks:** run in dark (translucent 0.15, blur) and light, with a simulated Claude on v2.
  - Diff card.
  - Permission card with its reason.
  - Pinned background command with live output.
  - Stopping it.
  - Sidebar count.
  - Nested sub-agent.
  - "Claude is working" while the task stays idle.
- **Earlier checks re-run:** sub-agent views and the main-agent checks, on the v1 path.
- **Real Claude Code (0.101, Haiku):**
  - End to end over v2 through Atrium's own connection: a Write and an Edit with their line counts, a background command, a foreground command, and a sub-agent in its own child session.
  - The background command was listed, its output arrived live line by line (the first line replacing the "running in background" notice), and it left the list when it exited.
  - The switch back to v1 worked against the real adapter.
  - Mid-turn messages, v1 and v2 side by side: both took effect once the running command finished, 4.7 s on v1 and 4.9 s on v2, and both skipped the remaining commands.

## Not verified

- With the real Claude Code:
  - "Claude is working": Claude's own turn after a background task. It was only seen with the simulated Claude. In the real runs, the task ended during a turn and Claude folded it in.

title: Atrium 0.13.6
notes:
From this version on, every new task can dispatch workers by default, and nothing needs to be switched on first. Whether to dispatch is the model's call; Atrium never asks you. Which agent and model may be dispatched, and how many at once, is enforced by the background service, so the same rules hold whatever agent the main task runs on.

## Main agent

- **On by default.** Tasks you create (new tasks, "Continue", "Hand off to another agent", presets) get the worker tools by default, on agents that support MCP: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity. The "Main agent" switch in the New Task panel is gone. Older tasks get the tools the next time they open, with no migration. A worker is still an ordinary task and can't dispatch workers of its own.
- **Kiro doesn't take part.** Kiro tasks get no worker tools, and a main agent can't dispatch Kiro either. Kiro keeps using its own sub-agents. The Atrium agent can't be a main agent for now, because it doesn't support MCP yet; it can be dispatched as a worker.
- **The sidebar shows "Main agent" only when there are workers.** A task that has never dispatched a worker looks like any other task. A main task with running workers gets a "Stop All Workers" item in its right-click menu, which stops and closes all of its workers without affecting the main task's own turn.

## Worker rules (enforced by the background service)

- **Allowed models.** Each agent has a list of models that may be dispatched, each marked Allowed, Sparingly or Not allowed. Defaults:
  - Claude Code: Sonnet and Haiku allowed; Opus sparingly.
  - Antigravity: Gemini 3.8 Flash only.
  - Codex: any model.
  - Atrium agent: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash only.
  - Kiro and agents not on the list: can't be dispatched.

  Models match by family (Sonnet, Haiku, Opus), so the list doesn't need changing when a model version is upgraded. With no model given, the first allowed model on the list is used. Dispatching a model off the list fails, and the error lists the models that can be used. Model values that don't say which model they are, such as "default" and "auto", are always refused.
- **Sparingly (Opus).** At most 1 at a time across all tasks, and the main agent has to state a reason when dispatching. The reason appears on the worker's hover tooltip and in the task inspector.
- **No model change mid-way.** `/model` and option changes that the main agent sends a worker are refused. If a worker's model drifts outside the list, the background service stops it, and the main agent learns why. A model change you make yourself in the worker's settings counts.
- **Limits.**
  - Each main task can have at most 4 workers running at once.
  - Across all tasks, at most 8 workers run at once.
  - Each turn can create at most 4 workers, closed ones included, so a create-then-close loop can't get around the limit.
  - Errors over a limit tell the main agent to wait, or to close workers first.
- **Unchanged:** while the main task is fenced, its workers stay fenced too.

## Settings

- New **Settings › Workers** page:
  - A global switch at the top, "Tasks can create workers" (on by default). Turning it off affects tasks opened afterwards; tasks already open keep their tools until they reopen.
  - Per agent: "Can direct workers" and "Can be dispatched" (not allowed, any model, or chosen models).
  - With "Chosen models", each model has its own Not allowed, Allowed or Sparingly setting. The Atrium agent's models carry their provider's name. A model on the list that the agent no longer offers shows "Unavailable".

## Compatibility

- Background service protocol 9 → 10.
- An older app connecting to this background service only sees "Main agent" on tasks that have workers.
- A remote that is still an older background service greys out this page and reads "Needs a newer background service".

## Tests

- **Unit tests:**
  - Default rules.
  - Family matching, including refusal of "default" and "auto".
  - The order of refusals: main agent, then target agent, then model, then limits.
  - Sparingly needing a reason and capped at one.
  - All three limits.
  - Refusal of `/model` and option changes from the main agent.
  - Drift outside the list stopping the worker.
  - The policy can't be changed from an agent connection.
  - Old tasks getting the tools when they reopen.
- **Full test suite:** passes in both modes, 1625 tests each.
- **Real-app screenshot checks:** run in dark (translucent 0.15, blur) and light.
  - No main-agent switch in the New Task panel.
  - "Main agent" appears only after the first worker.
  - A Kiro task gets no tools.
  - A main agent dispatching in a loop is refused at the 5th worker.
  - "Stop All Workers" closes both workers while the main task keeps running.
  - Default settings on the Workers page.
- The original main-agent and sub-agent view checks were re-run and pass.

## Not verified

- No real Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity has acted as a main agent dispatching a worker yet; the screenshot checks used simulated agents. After this version installs, the next time I (Claude Code, running inside Atrium) reopen, I get these tools, and I'll check right away.
- The Atrium agent's real provider list wasn't checked: if no provider on your Mac offers DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, it shows as "Unavailable" in Settings, and dispatching it fails.

title: Atrium 0.13.5
notes:
这一版是两项小修。回复里用 `*…*` 强调的中文改用楷体，不再和正文分不出来；harness 授权自检的提示也改了：v0.13.4 里那句「重启后台服务」是错的，现在改成正确的处理办法。

## 对话

- **中文强调用楷体。** 回复里的 `*强调*` 本来靠斜体显示。苹方没有斜体，macOS 也不会把中文变斜，所以强调里的中文看起来和正文一模一样，只有英文是斜的。现在强调里的中文、日文和全角标点改用楷体，字号比正文大 2 pt（楷体字面偏小，放大后才和正文一样高），行高不变；英文照旧是斜体。粗体（`**…**`）和粗斜体不变。标题里的楷体用常规字重：楷体的粗体字形会把行撑高。对话字体选「等宽」时不受影响：自带的 Maple Mono NF CN 有斜体，中文本来就是斜的。楷体是 macOS 的可下载字体，没装的话保持原样，Atrium 也不会去下载它。

## 开发与测试

- harness 授权自检（`harness.py preflight`）在缺授权时只给一条建议：去「系统设置 › 隐私与安全性」授权；如果 Atrium 已经在列表里、开关也开着，说明那是旧构建留下的条目，用「−」删掉再用「+」加回。v0.13.4 认为「后台服务比 Atrium 活得久时，授权传不到它下面」，并提示去重启后台服务。这个判断不对：后台服务脱离 Atrium 单独运行时，授权照样有效。所以那条提示和 `orphanedHelper` 诊断字段都去掉了。

## 兼容

- 后台服务协议版本不变（9）。

## 测试

- 单元测试：强调里只有中日韩字符和全角标点换成楷体，字号是所在文字的字号加 2；英文、粗体、粗斜体和行内代码不变；等宽字体或没装楷体时原样输出；本机装了楷体时，17 pt 楷体的行高不超过 15 pt 苹方。
- 全量测试两种模式（普通、严格）各跑一遍，全部通过。真实 app 的字阶截图检查在深色（半透明 0.15、模糊）和浅色下各跑一遍，都通过。另外用 Atrium 的 Markdown 组件离屏渲染了样张，标题、正文、列表、引用里强调的中文是楷体，英文仍是斜体，粗体、粗斜体和行内代码不变。

## 没有验证的

- 「更新后授权不再丢」：v0.13.4 起发布包用固定签名身份，这是第一次从固定签名的版本更新上来。要等你更新到这一版后再查一次辅助功能和录屏授权才能确认。

title: Atrium 0.13.4
notes:
这一版是几项小修：接手一个断开的会话时，带过去的「父任务结论」是它最后的回复，而不是适配器的报错输出；子 agent 的只读视图不再显示空的「上下文」；你发出的提示词和对话正文用同一种字体。

## 对话

- **父任务结论取最后一条回复。** 从一个已经断开的会话「继续」或「交给另一个 agent」时，新任务开头的「父任务结论」以前取的是会话结束的原因。agent 进程退出时，这个原因就是适配器的报错输出（`[idle-compaction] skip…`、`Unexpected case: {…}` 之类），对新任务没有用。现在取父会话最后一条助手消息；如果最后一轮没有正常结束（出错、被停止、被打断），结论后面加一行「父任务最后一轮没有正常结束；以上是它最后的回复」，报错输出不会带过去。任务检查器里照旧显示最后一轮的结果。
- **提示词不再用衬线体。** 你发出的提示词以前固定用衬线体（Charter 配宋体），回复和输入框用的是对话字体。现在提示词和对话正文同一种字体（默认系统字体配苹方），字重略重（medium），打字时和发出去以后看起来一样。设置 › 外观里换了对话字体，提示词也跟着换。选中任务的标题仍用衬线体。

## 子 agent

- 选中 Claude Code 子 agent 的只读视图时，右栏不再显示「上下文」：子 agent 没有自己的上下文读数，那一块一直是空的。右栏只剩「文件夹」。

## 修复

- 目录监听在一种时序下会和取消它的任务互相等待而卡住（取消时 Swift 运行时持有任务的锁，监听队列正好在把一次变化交给同一个任务）。正式 app 连着后台服务时不走这条路；测试和不连后台服务的演示模式会偶发卡死，测试套件在严格模式下卡住过一次。现在取消时不再等监听队列。
- 从终端派给其他 agent 的任务（`atrium-probe --learn`，总管派活用的就是它）会出现在时间线里，但点开是空的：它只记了和 agent 之间的原始收发，没有记对话。现在它像 Atrium 自己的任务一样记下每条提示词和 agent 的回复，派出去的任务在时间线里能看到完整过程；以前留下的、只有原始收发的那些不再列出。

## 开发与测试

- harness 开跑前先检查辅助功能和录屏两项授权（`scripts/test-app/harness.py preflight`，只用 `AXIsProcessTrusted()` 和 `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()`，从不弹授权、从不截屏），缺了就以退出码 3 停下，说明该给哪个 app 授权。后台服务比拉起它的 Atrium 活得久时（Atrium 重启过、后台服务还是旧的那个），给 Atrium 授权到不了它下面的进程，这时提示改为重启后台服务。
- 新增单测确保脚本里的截图都只截指定窗口（`screencapture -l`），没有全屏截图。

## 签名：授权不再随更新丢失

- 以前每个版本都是临时签名（ad hoc），macOS 按每次构建的哈希记住授权，所以每次更新后辅助功能、录屏和钥匙串里的「始终允许」都会失效。这一版起，发布包用一个固定的签名身份（自签名证书「Atrium Signing」）签名，包里的几个小程序也有了固定的标识（`io.github.chenkeyv.atrium.daemon` 等），以后更新时 macOS 都认得出是同一个 Atrium。
- **装上这一版后要再授权最后一次**：如果你给 Atrium 开过辅助功能或录屏，请在「系统设置 › 隐私与安全性」里把旧的 Atrium 删掉（「−」）再加回来（「+」）。钥匙串里记住的 SSH 密码第一次被读取时，macOS 会问一次是否允许，选「始终允许」。之后的更新都不会再问。
- 签名不是 Apple 的 Developer ID，没有经过公证。第一次在一台新 Mac 上打开时的提示，和以前一样。

## 兼容

- 后台服务协议版本不变（9）。

## 测试

- 单元测试：交接内容在连接断开、出错、停止、被打断后都取最后一条回复，不含报错输出；正常结束的交接不加那一行说明；提示词字体随对话字体族变化；取消正在迭代的目录监听任务时，即使监听队列被占着也立刻返回（旧代码上两种模式都失败），监听事件密集到来时反复取消也不卡；派活工具的会话有对话记录时才进时间线。两种模式全量测试通过，严格模式下目录监听测试连续 50 次通过、没有一次卡住。
- 签名：发布构建的每个可执行文件的指定要求都是「固定标识 + 这张证书」，`codesign --verify --deep --strict` 通过。

## 没有验证的

- 这一版发布前没有跑真实 app 的截图检查（harness）：截图要用辅助功能和录屏授权，而授权要等装上这一版、重新授权以后才稳定。子 agent 视图不显示「上下文」、提示词换成正文字体这两处改动，会在装上这一版后补跑截图确认，有问题在 v0.13.5 修。
- 「更新后授权不再丢」要到下一次更新（v0.13.5）时才能真正确认。
